Allyship is a set of small, repeatable habits. Pick the ones you will actually do — or write your own.

What can I do today?

Allyship that travels everywhere

Ask, don't assume

  • “What helps you focus?” beats guessing.
  • Accept the answer without negotiating it.

Make the invisible explicit

  • Agendas before meetings.
  • Written follow-ups after verbal decisions.

Offer options, not exceptions

  • Camera-optional calls, quiet rooms, flexible hours by default.
  • Adjustments nobody has to request are the best kind.

Judge output, not style

  • Fidgeting, pauses and unusual routes to an answer are not performance signals.

Sources & learning

Sources and Learning

Walk In My World uses general educational information from recognized organizations to inform its prototype content. These resources do not define every individual experience, and the organizations listed have not reviewed, approved, sponsored, or endorsed this prototype.

Responsible-use notes

  • Simulations and interpretations are brief artistic material. They cannot reproduce a lived experience and are never diagnostic.
  • Every person's experience differs — a perspective here is one possible experience, not a universal definition.
  • This prototype gives no diagnosis, no assessment, no score and no medical advice, and it never profiles a person.
  • No listed organization created, reviewed, validated, endorsed or sponsored this prototype.
